title: On-Prem VPC Modernization — Quickstart & Migration Notes
content:
Purpose
This is a compact hands-on quickstart and migration playbook for modernizing customer on-prem/VPC deployments so they match Redwood's current networking patterns and Terraform module model. Target audience: SREs on the delivery team, infra engs helping a tenant cutover, and SEs preparing the customer kickoff.

Scope (what this doc is intended to cover)
- Baseline pattern: dual-HA on-prem VPC connected to Redwood private plane via direct cross-connect or IPSec/BGP.
- Minimal working Terraform module mapping and recommended variable bindings for rapid onboarding.
- Stepwise migration plan (discovery -> pilot -> waves -> full cutover) and rollback guardrails.
- Smoke tests and monitoring checks to validate correctness post-cutover.
- Notes on state migration, version pinning, and compatibility pitfalls observed in previous projects.

High-level design assumptions (keep short)
- Customer provides: 2-edge routers (BGP capable), a private peering VLAN, and a route reflector or equivalent for BGP advertisements.
- We assume a dedicated tenant VPC on Redwood side with its own /22 (adjustable) and an advertised on-prem summary /16 or smaller prefixes.
- TLS + mTLS for control-plane connections; egress must pass through customer-managed NAT if policy requires.

Quickstart checklist (one-page actionable)
- Pre-kickoff
  - Collect ASN numbers (customer and redwood), proposed peer IPs, VLAN IDs, expected CIDR(s), and maintenance windows.
  - Create Jira ticket: NET-<customer>-BGP with required contacts and A/C.
  - Decide on Terraform backend: s3/encrypted bucket + dynamodb lock, or remote-backend accepted by customer.

- Staging (low-risk sandbox)
  - Clone rdw-vpc-core module at tag v1.4.2 (see module notes below).
  - Create workspace: terraform workspace set <customer>-staging.
  - Apply minimal infra: rdw_vpc_core.network (vlan, routes, radp placeholders), rdw_vpc_connectors.bgp with dry-run flag.
  - Validate BGP sessions establish and routes are exchanged.

- Pilot (single-app cutover)
  - Pick non-critical route table and a single service to route via new path.
  - Coordinate cutover window + monitor CPU/latency.
  - Run smoke tests and canary traffic for 4 hours, escalate if packet loss > 0.5% or latency > baseline + 25%.

- Wave migration
  - Group apps by risk (low/medium/high) and migrate in waves.
  - Keep rollback target ready (ip route and route-maps) to restore previous paths within 15 minutes.

- Closure
  - Decommission old tunnels once all traffic confirmed.
  - Finalize terraform state: move resources into prod workspace and tag versions.

Terraform module quick notes
- Recommended module map (logical names)
  - rdw-vpc-core: creates tenant VPC layout, route tables, subnet mapping, flow logs.
  - rdw-vpc-connectors: BGP/IPSec configuration, peer objects, route filters, BFD where supported.
  - rdw-egress-proxy: optional egress NAT/gateway appliances and DNAT rules for internet-bound service.
  - rdw-monitoring-bundle: Flow log export, alerting hooks (PagerDuty), and interface-level metrics.

- Variable conventions (example)
  - tenant_name: string -> kebab case (e.g., acme-corp-prod)
  - redwood_asn: number -> 64512
  - customer_asn: number -> provided by customer
  - allowed_cidrs: list(string) -> list of prefixes customer announces
  - bgp_hold_time: number -> 90 (defaults)

- Backend/state guidance
  - Use a customer-specific remote backend to keep state separation (s3://redwood-terraform-states/<customer>/).
  - Locking: dynamodb table name pattern tf-lock-<customer>. Always verify lock cleanup after failed runs.
  - State import: when switching from legacy scripts, use terraform import to adopt the BGP peer objects and route tables; avoid re-creation of physical interfaces.

- Versioning and upgrade policy
  - Pin modules to minor release (e.g., v1.4.2) during pilot. Upgrade cadence: minor every 6–8 weeks, major after test window.
  - Always run terraform plan in a pre-prod workspace and diff with a baseline plan plugin (compare-plans.sh) before apply.

Migration commute pitfalls seen previously
- Implicit dependency on cloud-provider-managed NAT gateways that customers don't mirror on-prem -> causes asymmetric routing.
- BGP community stripping by customer edge devices resulting in blackholed subnets; pre-check with show ip bgp neighbor x advertised-routes.
- Terraform state drift where manual console edits aren't captured -> add a pre-cutover inventory and import expected resources.
- MTU mismatch on cross-connects (jumbo frames) causing TLS handshake failures for large control-plane messages.

Runbook excerpts (commands and checks)
- BGP session check (customer router)
  - show ip bgp summary | grep <redwood-peer-ip>
  - expected: State = ESTABLISHED, prefixes received > 0 (for production).

- Healthcheck curl from infra jump host
  - curl -v --resolve api.<customer>.redwood.ai:<port>:<private-ip> https://api.<customer>.redwood.ai/healthz
  - expect 200 and latency under baseline.

Smoke tests (automated)
- Connectivity: run a 5-minute tcpdump on the egress interface and ensure SYN/SYN-ACK pairs complete for canary endpoints.
- Application-level: hit a small set of representative endpoints and validate JSON schema + stable tokenization timings for LLM inference calls.

Rollback playbook (fast rollback within window)
- If route leak or packet loss detected > threshold:
  - 1) Remove new BGP advertisements from the redwood peer (rdw-vpc-connectors.apply --disable-advertise).
  - 2) Re-establish previous path via pre-configured backup tunnel: terraform workspace select <customer>-backup && terraform apply -target=rdw_vpn.tunnel_backup -auto-approve
  - 3) Notify network ops and open incident with priority=sev2.

Monitoring and observability requirements
- Flow logs: enable at subnet level and ship to customer S3 or Redpanda as they require.
- Tracing: annotate flows with route-id tags so we can correlate latency spikes to specific route changes.
- Alerts: PagerDuty for BGP session down, >5% packet loss, or BGP prefix withdrawal of >10% of expected prefixes.

On-prem hardware compatibility hints
- Edge OS tested: IOS-XE (>=17.3), Junos (>=20.4), Nokia SR OS recent. For older boxes, avoid BFD and set bgp timers higher.
- If customer uses non-BGP overlay (e.g., SD-WAN), we need a small translator appliance — plan for an additional NAT/route-reflector leg.

Open questions / decisions to lock before kickoff
- Does the customer accept remote Terraform backend in Redwood account, or do they require customer-managed backend?
- Will the tenant require egress via customer firewall (adds NAT hop) or via Redwood-managed egress?
- Change freeze window preferences and escalation path for late-night rollbacks.

Appendix: short examples
- sample tf snippet for bgp peer (pseudo)
  module "rdw_vpc_connectors" {
    source = "github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules//rdw-vpc-connectors?ref=v1.4.2"
    tenant_name = var.tenant_name
    customer_asn = var.customer_asn
    redwood_asn = var.redwood_asn
    peer_ips = var.peer_ips
    advertise_cidrs = var.allowed_cidrs
  }

- quick verification checklist (post-apply)
  - BGP ESTABLISHED on both sides
  - All expected prefixes present in RIB and FIB
  - No unexpected route aggregates or more-specific leaks
  - Application-level healthcheck pass for canary services

Notes to self (informal)
- Try to push a small automation to fail-open for non-critical routes so we can recover more gracefully.
- Add a small preflight CLI tool to normalize customer inputs (ASN, CIDR, mtu) and emit a terraform vars file.
- Capture a short runbook video for SE handoff — folks always prefer a 5-min visual demo.

References and previous run links
- internal lab notes: lab/acme-onprem-2024 (private)
- example migration playbook (older): https://drive.redwood.ai/migrations/onprem-legacy-cutovers

End of quickstart. Keep this doc lightweight — convert into a formal playbook and templates once we validate with two pilots.
